slides.title: GPT: Generative Pre-trained Transformer

ul: A transformer is a type of neural network architecture designed to process sequences of information using attention.
It was introduced in the 2017 paper “Attention Is All You Need”.
Before transformers, sequence models commonly used architectures such as RNNs and LSTMs, which processed text more sequentially.

body: In 2017, Google researchers published “Attention Is All You Need”. Their transformer reads all the tokens at once, and attention links any two words directly, however far apart they are.

slides.title: The loop: how a model writes an answer
slides.summary: The model predicts one token, adds it to the text, and runs again on the longer text. It stops when its best guess is the end token.
body: Give the model “The pizza is ready” and ask what comes next. Each run of the model does the same job: turn the text into vectors, pass them through the transformer's layers, and score every possible next token. The second figure below shows one run in full.

ul: Run 1 reads “The pizza is ready” and picks “ for”.
Append it. The input is now “The pizza is ready for”, one token longer.
Run 2 reads all of that, including the word it just wrote, and picks “ you”. Then “!”, one token per run.

body: <mark>The model never writes a whole answer at once. Every token comes from a full run over everything so far, including the tokens it has already written.</mark>

body.h: How does it know it's finished?

body: It doesn't decide in any deep sense. Every answer in its training data ended with a special end token, so once a reply looks complete, that token becomes the most likely prediction. When it wins, the loop stops.

ul: The end token wins: the usual way a reply ends.
A length limit: the app caps the number of tokens, which can cut a reply off mid-sentence.
A stop sequence: the app can also stop when a chosen piece of text appears.

body.text: Inside every run, attention lets the newest token look back at everything before it. That's what makes the model's guesses fit the context, and it's the subject of the next chapter.

body.more: Isn't re-reading the whole text every run slow?
body.text: It would be. Models keep the work already done for earlier tokens in a KV cache, so each run only has to compute the newest token.
body.link: The KV cache in Output & inference

body.more: What does the end token look like?
body.text: It's one of the tokenizer's special tokens, such as <|endoftext|> in GPT-2. Chat models use an end-of-turn token from their chat template.

steps.caption: The model gets the token IDs of the text so far.

figure.alt: The generation loop for "The pizza is ready". Run 1 reads The, pizza, is, ready and predicts " for" at 42%; it is appended. Run 2 reads the five tokens and predicts " you" at 58%; appended. Run 3 reads six tokens and predicts "!" at 47%; appended. Run 4 reads "The pizza is ready for you!" and predicts the special end token at 81%, so the loop stops and the reply is finished. Finishing is just one more prediction: answers in training ended with an end token, so the model learns to predict it once a reply is complete. Apps also stop at a length limit. Probabilities are illustrative.
figure.caption: Each run's winner joins the input for the next run. The reply ends when the end token wins.

figure.alt: How an LLM predicts the next token for "The pizza is ready". 1: split into tokens The, space pizza, space is, space ready. 2: look up token IDs, 791, 23317, 374 and 5644 in GPT-4. 3: turn IDs into vectors of numbers, plus position. 4: run the transformer: N identical layers, each with layer norm, self-attention, where ready looks back at every earlier token, layer norm and a feed-forward network; then layer norm and linear plus softmax, giving one score per vocabulary token. Self-attention is the subject of the next chapter. 5: score every possible token, for 42%, to 31%, at 12%, now 6%, and pick one, giving The pizza is ready for. 6: add it to the text and run again, one token at a time. Values are illustrative.
figure.caption: One run in full, from text to the next token. Attention, the highlighted box, is the next chapter.
